hook: A set of internal Air Materiel Command memos and correspondence from August–December 1947 documenting the Air Force's earliest systematic investigation of flying saucer reports, culminating in General Curtis LeMay's formal written confirmation that no U.S. research project could account for the observed phenomena.
why_it_matters: The August 22, 1947 Garrett analysis contained in this file is historically significant as one of the earliest official attempts to extract consistent physical characteristics from credible witness reports — and the follow-on response signed by LeMay explicitly rules out a domestic U.S. origin, eliminating a major alternative explanation on the record. The December 1947 McCoy correspondence shows AMC Intelligence was still pressing Air Force headquarters for a response and formal project authorization months after these reports, revealing institutional friction about how seriously to treat the phenomenon. Together, these documents trace the bureaucratic chain that led directly to the formation of Project Sign.

key_findings.finding: General Curtis LeMay, Deputy Chief of Air Staff for Research and Development, formally confirmed in writing that the Army Air Forces had no research project matching the physical characteristics of reported flying saucers, ruling out U.S. origin.

quotes.text: The Army Air Forces has no research project with the characteristics described in Comment No. 1.

key_findings.finding: Lt. Col. Garrett's August 1947 analysis of credible flying saucer reports identified a consistent set of physical characteristics: metallic surface, circular and slightly domed shape, size comparable to a C-54 or Constellation, speeds above 300 knots, formations of three to nine objects, a blue-brown exhaust trail consistent with a throttleable liquid rocket engine, and lateral oscillation during flight.

quotes.text: Surface is metallic - indicating a metallic skin, at least.
As to shape, all observations state that the object is circular, or at jeast elliptical, flat on the bottom and slightly domed on the top.
Flights have been reported containing from three to nine objects, flying good formation on each other, with speeds always above 300 knots.

When a trail is observed, it is a lightly colored blue—brown haze, similar to a rocket engine's exhaust. Contrary to a rocket of the solid type, one observation indicates that the fuel may be throttled, which would indicate a liquid rocket engine.

key_findings.finding: As of December 1947, AMC Intelligence under Colonel H.M. McCoy was still receiving no response from Air Force headquarters to its earlier flying disc correspondence, and characterized continued reports from qualified observers as an active concern requiring ongoing collection and analysis.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: Air Materiel Command at Wright Field, Dayton, Ohio is the originating and primary organizational actor throughout every document in this file.

The project mandated in this file — Priority 2A collection and analysis of sighting reports at AMC — is the direct institutional precursor to Project Sign, which launched in early 1948 and evolved into Projects Grudge and Blue Book.

The explicit request for FBI background investigations of civilian flying disc witnesses indicates early coordination between military intelligence and domestic law enforcement on UAP-related counterintelligence concerns.
